title: Uniqueness of universal first order thickenings
statement: Let $R,S,U,V$ be commutative rings, with $S,U,V$ commutative $R$-algebras. Let $p:U\to S$ and $q:V\to S$ be surjective $R$-algebra homomorphisms with $(\ker p)^2=(\ker q)^2=0$. Assume that for $W=U$ with $r=p$ and for $W=V$ with $r=q$, every commutative $R$-algebra $A$, ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$, and $R$-algebra homomorphism $a:S\to A/I$ admit exactly one $R$-algebra homomorphism $b:W\to A$ satisfying $\operatorname{quot}_I\circ b=a\circ r$. Then there is exactly one $R$-algebra isomorphism $e:U\cong V$ with $q\circ e=p$. No formally unramified hypothesis on $S$ is required.

source.place: Algebra, Section 04EA (section-conormal), uniqueness remark after Lemma 04EB; the universal-property argument works without formal unramifiedness.

proof.text: *Uniqueness up to unique isomorphism.* Let $(S'_1,\pi_1)$, $(S'_2,\pi_2)$ both have the properties of the statement, with kernels $K_1,K_2$. Apply the universal property of $(S'_1,\pi_1)$ to $A=S'_2$, $I=K_2$ and $a=\bar\pi_2^{-1}:S\to S'_2/K_2$, the inverse of the isomorphism $\bar\pi_2:S'_2/K_2\to S$ induced by $\pi_2$: the condition $q\circ\phi=a\circ\pi_1$ on an $R$-algebra map $\phi:S'_1\to S'_2$ is $\pi_2\circ\phi=\pi_1$, so there is exactly one such $\phi$. Likewise exactly one $\psi:S'_2\to S'_1$ with $\pi_1\circ\psi=\pi_2$. Then $\psi\circ\phi$ and $\mathrm{id}_{S'_1}$ both satisfy $\pi_1\circ(-)=\pi_1$, so by the uniqueness for $(S'_1,\pi_1)$ applied to $A=S'_1$, $I=K_1$, $a=\bar\pi_1^{-1}$, $\psi\circ\phi=\mathrm{id}$; symmetrically $\phi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}$. So $\phi$ is the unique isomorphism of $R$-algebras compatible with the maps to $S$. In Lean, convert the lifting equation by Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective, then construct the inverse pair with AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom.

theorem universalFirstOrderThickening_unique
    (R S S' : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra R S']
    (π : S' →ₐ[R] S) (hπ : Function.Surjective π)
    (hker : RingHom.ker π.toRingHom ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hprop : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ →
      ∀ a : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I,
        ∃! a' : S' →ₐ[R] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp a' = a.comp π)
    (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [Algebra R T] (πT : T →ₐ[R] S)
    (hπT : Function.Surjective πT) (hkerT : RingHom.ker πT.toRingHom ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hT : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ →
      ∀ a : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I,
        ∃! a' : T →ₐ[R] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp a' = a.comp πT) :
    ∃! e : S' ≃ₐ[R] T, πT.comp e.toAlgHom = π
